subject: general
question:
Where can we find such cells with thickened cell walls in a plant?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/058bbcacc7ac0f6fb68cece1919f6976af5deb6675f2c7b07c6cb0ddaaa8d72c.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __**In meristem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In Meristem**

 
 
• Meristems are the growth regions of plants, composed of undifferentiated cells capable of continuous cell division.
 
• These cells have a large nucleus, dense cytoplasm, and lack prominent vacuoles.
 
• Meristems are responsible for primary growth (length) and secondary growth (width) in plants.
 
• They are classified into apical, lateral, and intercalary meristems based on their location and function.
 
• Apical meristems are found at the tips of roots and shoots, promoting primary growth.
 
• Lateral meristems, like the vascular cambium, are responsible for secondary growth by producing new xylem and phloem cells.
 
• Intercalary meristems are found at the base of nodes or internodes in some plants, contributing to growth in length.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In Phloem**

 
 
• Phloem is a complex tissue responsible for transporting sugars, amino acids, and other organic compounds produced by photosynthesis from leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibers.
 
• Sieve tube elements are elongated cells with perforated end walls called sieve plates, facilitating the flow of phloem sap.
 
• Companion cells are specialized cells that support and regulate the metabolic activities of sieve tube elements.
 
• Phloem parenchyma cells store food and provide structural support.
 
• Phloem fibers provide mechanical support to the plant.
 
 
 
• **In Epidermis**
 
 
• The epidermis is the outermost layer of cells that covers and protects the plant body.
 
• It forms a barrier against water loss, pathogens, and physical damage.
 
• Epidermal cells are typically flattened and covered with a waxy cuticle that reduces water loss.
 
• Specialized epidermal cells include guard cells, which regulate gas exchange through stomata, and trichomes, which may have various functions like defense, reducing water loss, or increasing surface area.
 
• In some plants, the epidermis may be modified to form root hairs, which increase the surface area for water and mineral absorption.
 
 
 
• **In Xylem**
 
 
• Xylem is a complex tissue responsible for transporting water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of tracheids, vessel elements, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibers.
 
• Tracheids are elongated cells with lignified cell walls, providing structural support and facilitating water conduction.
 
• Vessel elements are wider and shorter than tracheids, forming continuous tubes for efficient water transport.
 
• Xylem parenchyma cells store food and provide structural support.
 
• Xylem fibers provide mechanical support to the plant.
